question: The EU strategy for islands (COM(2026)0520) recognises the structural and permanent handicaps of island regions, recalling Article 174 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. In Sicily, these disadvantages affect mobility, transport and energy costs.

Although some sectoral measures have been taken, there is still no national or regional structural mechanism specifically designed to compensate Sicilian citizens and businesses for the higher costs associated with the island condition.

This situation is particularly relevant in the light of Article 119 of the Italian Constitution, which recognises the particularities of the islands and provides for measures to remove the disadvantages resulting from insularity. Can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
What EU cohesion and financial instruments can help mitigate these increased costs?
What margins do the State aid rules offer for national or regional compensatory measures?

In the implementation of the EU strategy for islands and in the post-2027 programming period, does the Commission intend to provide for specific instruments to structurally compensate for the handicaps of island regions?
